subject: Post-demo: quality variance observed after model distro update — decision ladder & timelines
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@crestbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Quick recap + next steps after demo — observed quality variance

Hi Samir / Elaine,

Thanks again for the demo time today — appreciated the walkthrough of the decisioning flows and the example prompts. As promised, a short recap and immediate next steps:

- What we talked about: integration approach, latency targets, token budgets, and the two key intents (transaction classification, refund justification summarization).
- Immediate ask from your side: you flagged that some outputs you saw in production this week look different than the demo last month (more hallucination on refund explanations).
- My commitment: investigate variance, snapshot the model variants you're on, and prepare an eval pack showing token-by-token diffs plus a rollback/pinning recommendation.

I'm attaching a short sample-outputs.txt excerpt you sent during the call (redacted PII). Can you confirm whether the production host is crest-prod-va1 and whether the deploy that landed last Wednesday was labeled v2.1-release? That will help narrow the scope.

Proposed next steps (timeline):
1) Today — confirm prod host + attach any extra failing examples (Samir).
2) EOD tomorrow — Redwood ops will run a quick model diff snapshot against v2.0 (golden) vs v2.1 and share a triage summary (Marissa/Connor).
3) By next Tue — full eval pack (benchmarks, prompt set, prioritized failing examples) and a recommendation: canary rollback or pin to v2.0, plus fallback policy.

If this is urgent for your Q4 reporting, we can escalate to a hotfix window; let me know.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference

Thanks Tessa — attaching the two full examples we pulled from prod. We confirmed the host is crest-prod-va1 and the deploy note for last Wednesday mentions v2.1-release (build: 2026-11-03_23h).

Behavior summary:
- Refund justification: increased length and insertion of non-existent policy references in ~7% of sampled cases (examples attached).
- Classification edge cases: borderline language that previously mapped to code 302 now toggles between 302 and 999.

Impact: our fraud/risk queue is getting noise, and the finance team flagged it for the monthly ops review. We'd like a short-term pin to the previous snapshot if that's the safest option. Can you confirm the rollback window and any expected downtime/latency changes?

Samir
Sr. Product Manager — Payments, CrestBank

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Quick recap + next steps after demo — observed quality variance

Marissa / Connor — forwarding Samir's examples. TL;DR: customer sees clear delta after v2.1-release vs v2.0. They want a short-term pin/rollback and an eval pack for execs.

Initial internal checklist:
- Connor: can you run a model-output diff on crest-prod-va1 between snapshot:v2.0 (tag:crest-2026-09-01) and snapshot:v2.1 (tag:v2.1-release) for the two prompt sets Samir attached? Prioritize refund-justification prompt and the borderline classification set. Please include token-level alignment and BLEU/ROUGE where applicable.
- Marissa: assemble an eval pack (eval-pack.zip) with prompt sets, aggregated metrics (precision/recall, hallucination rate proxy), and a short executive summary aimed at Samir's COO. Add a recommendation: (A) pin to v2.0 for 72h with canary traffic at 10% for v2.1, or (B) staged rollback of v2.1 to v2.0 in crest-prod. Note risks and estimated cost delta.
- Ops/sre: log RID INF-4821 (linked) and prepare a quick rollback playbook (DB snapshot not needed; we are only rolling model artifact).

Decision ladder (what I'd present to the customer):
1) Contain: immediate pin to v2.0 if we confirm increased hallucination or misclassification at >5% error delta.
2) Observe: run the canary (10% traffic) for 24 hours to validate fix for the most common prompts.
3) Roll forward: if canary passes, reintroduce v2.1 with mitigations (prompt-safeguards + post-processing rules).
4) Escalate: if canary fails, proceed with staged rollback and open an engineering root-cause ticket.

Please reply with ETA on the diff and the eval pack. Samir: we'll share the EOD triage after Connor's diff.

Thanks,
Tessa

Attachment(s): (referenced after internal assembly)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 18:45:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Fwd: Quick recap + next steps after demo — observed quality variance

All — quick status and proposed timeline for CrestBank: 

Status:
- Connor completed the diff run on 2026-11-09 and posted results to INF-4821. Short summary: v2.1 shows a +6.8 percentage-point increase in hallucination proxies on refund prompts and a 4.2 point shift in classification F1 on the borderline set. Token alignment showed repeated insertion of a policy phrase token sequence not present in v2.0.
- Root cause hypothesis: a small prompt-conditioning change in the v2.1 tokenizer path combined with a subtle decoder bias introduced by the new attention-kernel switch.

Attachments included: eval-pack.zip (benchmarks, prompt sets, failing examples, suggested mitigation snippets).

Recommendation (optics + safety):
- Short-term: Pin CrestBank to snapshot:v2.0 for 72 hours while we run a mitigations branch. This is low risk operationally (no infra downtime) and reversible. We expect minimal latency impact.
- Mid-term: deploy a canary of v2.1 with prompt-safeguard wrappers (strip risky policy-phrases; add conservative decoding constraints) at 5% traffic for 24–48h. If metrics return to baseline, we can expand to 50% then full roll.
- If canary fails: staged rollback and a release block on the v2.1 line until the kernel/conditioning fix is validated.

Owner matrix and ETA:
- Connor: full diff report and token-level artifacts — delivered 2026-11-09 (link in INF-4821).
- Marissa: eval-pack.zip and exec summary — delivered 2026-11-16 (attached).
- Tessa: coordinate pin approval and customer comms — Action: send pin request template to CrestBank legal/ops by tomorrow morning.

Samir / Elaine — if you're aligned with the short-term pin, we'll schedule the pin for Wed 2026-11-18 02:00 UTC (low-traffic window). Please reply with approval or a requested different window.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Product, Redwood Inference

Attachment(s): eval-pack.zip
